name: Ancient Civilizations & Empires
description: Economic systems, institutions, infrastructure, and state power across ancient civilizations.
episode_objects: a grain-account tablet and sealed jar
a tax register beside a road and warehouse plan
time_place_scopes: a dated urban market and its hinterland
a trade corridor during a documented fiscal cycle
mechanisms: taxation, labor, and storage converting harvest into state capacity
credit, transport, and institutional rules allocating risk and surplus
evidence_lenses: inscriptions, accounts, archaeology, and comparative economic history
source criticism separating official claims from material evidence
exclusions: Do not reduce a civilization to a modern business or impose present-day national categories.
Do not invent precise prices, GDP, profit, or universal motives where evidence is incomplete.
prompt_context: Explain one historical economic mechanism through dated institutions, records, and material constraints. Keep causal claims evidence-led, distinguish state rhetoric from evidence, and avoid modern financial analogies that erase difference.
